composition: Twelve layers of aramid fabric treated with 20% phosphoric acid solution (0% denotes deionized water). E-51:Z-6018 mass ratio 6:4; modified epoxy:4-MHHPA:DMP-30 mass ratio 100:85.68:0.5. Final fabric/resin fraction unreported.
sample_state: P/EM 20% phosphoric acid treatment; initial cured 12-ply aramid fabric laminate
treatment_chemistry: Siloxane-modified epoxy with 20% phosphoric-acid-treated aramid fabric
treatment_method: Industrial aramid fabric from Tayho Advanced Materials was sequentially pretreated with toluene, acetone and deionized water in an HL-20 annular centrifugal extractor for a reported 3 h; whether this duration applies per liquid is not specified. The fabric was dried in a vacuum oven at 110 °C for 6 h. Fabric was then immersed in deionized water or the specified phosphoric acid solution at 40 °C for 24 h, repeatedly rinsed with deionized water to neutral and oven-dried at 80 °C for an unreported duration. E-51 epoxy and Z-6018 phenyl propyl polysiloxane were mixed at a 6:4 mass ratio using an unspecified amount of acetone, with a phosphazene catalyst of unspecified identity and loading, reacted at 15 °C for 5 h and rotary-evaporated for 2 h. The modified epoxy, 4-MHHPA and DMP-30 were mixed at 100:85.68:0.5 by mass and degassed at 70 °C and −0.08 MPa for 1 h. Twelve fabric layers were laid up by hand and cured in a JZ-5009 flat vulcanizing press at 5 MPa, 100 °C for 2 h and 150 °C for 5 h. Final fabric/resin mass or volume fractions, fabric areal density and weave are not reported.

Mix 5 kg banana peel with 20 L of 99% isopropanol in a vessel protected from air for 48 h at 900 rpm. Filter through Macherey-Nagel MN-GF-3 paper and heat to 85 °C to evaporate isopropanol and recover extraction precipitate. The drying value 750 °C is printed in the original and remains unresolved. Table 2 gives 12 g extract per 250 mL, consistent with the 48 g/L impregnation concentration stated in prose. Apply the stated impregnation or coating process, dry at 110 °C for 3 min, and fix at 150 °C for 2 min. Table 2 states no rinse. Impregnation uses a Prowhite horizontal pneumatic squeezing machine and coating an Ataç RGK-40 laboratory coating device; wet pickup, coating thickness and application dwell time are not reported.

source_title: Flame Retardancy of Cotton Fabric: Effect of Coating of Polymeric Film Containing Phosphorus by Admicellar Polymerization
source_location: Whole original six-page publisher article, pp 2908–2913, methods, Tables 1/2, Figures 1–3, conclusions and all references reviewed. Original recipe/method/Table 2/Figure 3 pixels inspected. No graph digitization.
limitations: Six independently reviewed treated source states. Table 2 gives exact measured LOI/T10 for matching fabric labels. The source calls T10wt% an onset; map it only to T10, not Tonset. All DTG column temperatures are retained in raw fields because the text does not separately define their maximum-rate and stage semantics; DTA endotherms and stage mass losses are excluded from canonical TG metrics. CF-PVPA-3 residue is held because Table 2, thermal prose and abstract say 28.2% at 600 °C but the conclusion says 28.2% at 60 °C; no typo correction, while its independent T10 remains available. Figure 3 has a Weight loss (%) axis label but descending curves start near 100; preserve the mislabeled-axis issue and do not derive values from its coordinates. The TG method explicitly describes nitrogen TG and Table 2 separates TG, DTG and DTA, yet the named instrument is DSCQ10 (DSC Thermal Analyzer); this unresolved instrument description is retained verbatim rather than corrected or replaced from another paper. Areal density 110 g/m² versus GSM 200 remains unresolved and the canonical density is blank. Cotton includes about 10% polyester; no exact 90/10 ratio is inferred. Original monomer units mM and reported phosphorus percentages are preserved without dosage or retained-add-on conversion. The AIBA 0.30 mM value occurs in the representative 0.30 mM monomer recipe; per-row initiator concentrations beyond that recipe and binding-agent quantity are unreported. The rinse belongs to preparation; no durability washing is reported in this paper. Table 1 P percentages are measured by the described digestion/spectrophotometric procedure; they are not coating mass add-ons. CF-Control repeats the exact LOI/T10/DTG/R600 tuple in related DOI 10.14233/ajchem.2022.23915 and remains separately reuse-held rather than being admitted twice. Distinct 2009 APP/PER/melamine states and a 2016 washable polyester/cotton control were included in the reuse audit; their unresolved source identifiers remain held. No assays or numeric values are borrowed from cited earlier studies.

limitations: Ten treated source states are extracted under the disclosed original-evidence limits. Only exact own measured LOI and explicit TG are used. Table 3 defines onset of degradation, with no fixed mass-loss threshold or maximum-rate equivalence inferred. The washed group has a 20 min DI-water wash at 40 °C, described also as 10 min × 2, two cold DI-water rinses in section 3.2, and 80 °C drying for 5 min. Repeated treatment counts represent complete treatment, cure, wash and weighing cycles, not extra independent durability washes. Fabric 2 is held for LOI 26 versus prose 27; fabric 10 LOI 27–28 is a range and is held. Fabric 1 has an exact numeric pair but its individual formulation/add-on row was not recovered, so it stays held. Fabric 14 residue is 27.1 in Table 3 versus indexed prose 271; no decimal repair is assumed. Fabric 14 consequently has no retained canonical TG and stays held. Fabric 11 is consistently the two-cycle sodium-carbonate state, but add-on is 14.5 ± 0.3 in Table 2/thermal discussion versus 13.9 in the FTIR discussion and SI Figure S5; no single canonical add-on is assigned. HCl is 2 N in the specific section 3.2 recipe versus generic 5% catalyst wording in section 2.2; both are retained without conversion. Control is held for conservative family QA: related AATCC Review 2012 gives the same LOI 21, same style #423 and TG method, with onset 337.7 and residue 0.36 versus this source 337.2 and 0.4. This near coincidence is not proof of identical measurements, and distinct treated chemistries are not excluded. material_form: plain woven jute fabric/PP laminate from woven-nonwoven textile preform
composition: 42 wt% jute fabric and 58 wt% PP matrix; 31 vol% reinforcing fibre (Table 1)
treatment_chemistry: Thermoplastic consolidation of needle-punched woven natural fabric and nonwoven polymer web; no flame-retardant chemical finish
treatment_method: Loomstate plain woven reinforcing fabric was combined with carded PP or PLA staple-fibre nonwoven webs using an Automatex carding machine followed by an Automatex needle-punching machine. Section 4.2 refers to a 40:60 w/w web/fabric feed, while the cited earlier preparation explicitly calls this woven fabric/thermoplastic fibre 40:60. This ordering ambiguity is retained; Table 1 separately reports the actual fibre/polymer composition for each laminate. Eight preform layers between aluminium plates were heated at 190 °C for 2.5 min at 20 kg/cm², then the plate-composite assembly was transferred to another water-cooled press for 2 min at 10 kg/cm². Jute and sisal fabrics were from NITTRAD, Bangladesh; wool supplier is unreported. PP staple fibres were 50 mm, 3.3 dtex; PLA fibres were 40 mm, 2.2 dtex. The source refers detailed needle settings to the 2018 preparation paper; these settings are not transferred into the own-method fields.
source_title: Effects of Water and Chemical Solutions Ageing on the Physical, Mechanical, Thermal and Flammability Properties of Natural Fibre-Reinforced Thermoplastic Composites
source_location: Published original 24-page article, Tables 1/3/4 and sections 2.3–2.4 and 4.1–4.6; institutional PDF and PMC original HTML. Related 2018 accepted manuscript separately reviewed for observation reuse.
limitations: Five unaged textile-laminate compositions are represented. All paired numerical values appear in the same original study. Four jute/sisal LOIs and composition rows also match the earlier 2018 preparation paper, which contains no TGA assay; these are repeated LOI observations, not independent LOI replicates. The later study provides the own experimental TG values. The earlier source therefore requires sample-scoped reuse exclusion for those four control names. Its LOI width and repetition details are not substituted for the later study methods. source_preparation: Plain-knitted PET fabric, 100 g/m2, Zhejiang Xinjian Textiles. Thermofixed fabric cleaned with NaOH 30 g/l at 90 C for 20 min and acetone Soxhlet for 24 h. Pretreated fabric soaked 24 h in acetone/monomer solution; source says quart glass; irradiated by Van De Graff 5 MeV electron accelerator in air at room temperature. Specific thermal/LOI aliquot absorbed dose and bath concentration are not identified. Figure 2 uses 200 kGy for a graft-yield study, not an automatically assigned assay dose. Post-irradiation boiling DI water 6 h, acetone Soxhlet 24 h, drying105 C24 h. These are preparation extractions, not durability laundering. Table1/figure captions identify DG55.4% AAc,25.98% AAm,10.9% DMVP as grafted/original mass gain; no inferred retained monomer fraction. Source generic monomer-concentration discussion and sample DG values are kept distinct.
